contents.html: The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analysis to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsibilities include the development of technical, physical, administrative, and management standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of sensitive unclassified information in Federal computer systems. This Special Publication 800-series reports on ITL’s research, guidance, and outreach efforts in computer security and its collaborative activities with industry, government, and academic organizations.
contents.html_ja: 米国国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の情報技術研究所（ITL）は、国家の計測・標準インフラに技術的リーダーシップを提供することで、米国経済と公共の福祉を促進している。ITLは、情報技術の発展と生産的な利用を推進するため、試験、試験方法、参照データ、概念実証実装、および技術分析を開発している。ITLの責務には、連邦コンピュータシステムにおける機微な非機密情報のセキュリティとプライバシーを費用対効果の高い方法で確保するための、技術的、物理的、事務的、および管理的な標準とガイドラインの策定が含まれる。この特別刊行物800シリーズは、コンピュータセキュリティに関するITLの研究、指針、普及活動、および産業界、政府、学術機関との協力活動について報告するものである。

Executive Summary

The Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) is a suite of specifications that standardize the format and nomenclature by which software flaw and security configuration information is communicated, both to machines and humans.1 SCAP is a multi-purpose framework of specifications that support automated configuration, vulnerability and patch checking, technical control compliance activities, and security measurement. Goals for the development of SCAP include standardizing system security management, promoting interoperability of security products, and fostering the use of standard expressions of security content.
SCAP version 1.2 is comprised of eleven component specifications in five categories:

Languages. The SCAP languages provide standard vocabularies and conventions for expressing security policy, technical check mechanisms, and assessment results. The SCAP language specifications are Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF), Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language (OVAL®), and Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL™).

Reporting formats. The SCAP reporting formats provide the necessary constructs to express collected information in standardized formats. The SCAP reporting format specifications are Asset Reporting Format (ARF) and Asset Identification. Although Asset Identification is not explicitly a reporting format, SCAP uses it as a key component in identifying the assets that reports relate to.

Enumerations. Each SCAP enumeration defines a standard nomenclature (naming format) and an official dictionary or list of items expressed using that nomenclature. The SCAP enumeration specifications are Common Platform Enumeration (CPE™), Common Configuration Enumeration (CCE™), and Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE®).
contents.html_ja: 列挙。各SCAP列挙は、標準的な命名法（命名形式）と、その命名法で表現された項目の公式な辞書または一覧を定義する。SCAP列挙仕様は、共通プラットフォーム列挙（CPE™）、共通構成列挙（CCE™）、および共通脆弱性識別子（CVE®）である。

contents.html: Measurement and scoring systems. In SCAP this refers to evaluating specific characteristics of a security weakness (for example, software vulnerabilities and security configuration issues) and, based on those characteristics, generating a score that reflects their relative severity. The SCAP measurement and scoring system specifications are Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) and Common Configuration Scoring System (CCSS).
contents.html_ja: 測定およびスコアリングシステム。SCAPにおいてこれは、セキュリティ上の弱点（たとえばソフトウェア脆弱性やセキュリティ構成の問題）の特性を評価し、その特性に基づいて相対的な深刻度を示すスコアを生成することを指す。SCAPの測定およびスコアリングシステムの仕様は、共通脆弱性評価システム（CVSS）および共通構成評価システム（CCSS）である。

contents.html: Integrity. An SCAP integrity specification helps to preserve the integrity of SCAP content and results. Trust Model for Security Automation Data (TMSAD) is the SCAP integrity specification.

SCAP utilizes software flaw and security configuration standard reference data. This reference data is provided by the National Vulnerability Database (NVD),2 which is managed by NIST and sponsored by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

This publication defines the technical composition of SCAP version 1.2 in terms of its component specifications, their interrelationships and interoperation, and the requirements for SCAP content. The technical specification for SCAP in this publication describes the requirements and conventions that are to be employed to ensure the consistent and accurate exchange of SCAP-conformant content and the ability to reliably use the content with SCAP-conformant products.

The U.S. Federal Government, in cooperation with academia and private industry, is adopting SCAP and encourages its use in support of security automation activities and initiatives.3 SCAP has achieved widespread adoption by major software manufacturers and has become a significant component of large information security management and governance programs. The protocol is expected to evolve and expand in support of the growing needs to define and measure effective security controls, assess and monitor ongoing aspects of that information security, and successfully manage systems in accordance with risk management frameworks such as NIST Special Publication 800-534, Department of Defense (DoD) Instruction 8500.2, and the Payment Card Industry (PCI) framework. By detailing the specific and appropriate usage of the SCAP 1.2 components and their interoperability, NIST encourages the creation of reliable and pervasive SCAP content and the development of a wide array of products that leverage SCAP. Organizations that develop SCAP 1.2-based content or products should comply with the following recommendations: Follow the requirements listed in this document and in the associated component specifications. Organizations should ensure that their implementation and use of SCAP 1.2 is compliant with the requirements detailed in each component specification and this document. If requirements are in conflict between component specifications, this document will provide clarification. If a component specification is in conflict with this document, the requirements in this document take precedence. When creating SCAP content, adhere to the conventions specified in this document. Security products and checklist authors assemble content from SCAP data repositories to create SCAP-conformant security guidance. For example, a security configuration checklist can document desired security configuration settings, installed patches, and other system security elements using a standardized SCAP format. Such a checklist would use XCCDF to describe the checklist, CCE to identify security configuration settings to be addressed or assessed, and CPE to identify platforms for which the checklist is valid. The use of CCE and CPE entries within XCCDF checklists is an example of an SCAP convention—a requirement for valid SCAP usage. These conventions are considered part of the definition of SCAP 1.2. Organizations producing SCAP content should adhere to these conventions to ensure the highest degree of interoperability. NIST provides an SCAP Content Validation Tool that organizations can use to help validate the correctness of their SCAP content. The tool checks that SCAP source and result content is well-formed, all cross references are valid, and required values are appropriately set.5

contents.html_ja: 1.2 目的および適用範囲

contents.html: This document provides the definitive technical specification for version 1.2 of the Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP). SCAP (pronounced ess-cap) consists of a suite of specifications for standardizing the format and nomenclature by which software flaw and security configuration information is communicated, both to machines and humans. This document defines requirements for creating and processing SCAP source content. These requirements build on the requirements defined within the individual SCAP component specifications. Each new requirement pertains either to using multiple component specifications together or to further constraining one of the individual component specifications. The requirements within the individual component specifications are not repeated in this document; see those specifications to view their requirements.
contents.html_ja: 本文書は、Security Content Automation Protocol（SCAP）バージョン1.2の正式な技術仕様を示す。SCAP（「エスキャップ」と発音する）は、ソフトウェアの欠陥およびセキュリティ設定に関する情報を機械と人間の双方に伝達する際の形式と命名法を標準化するための仕様群から成る。本文書は、SCAPソースコンテンツの作成および処理に関する要件を定める。これらの要件は、個々のSCAP構成要素仕様で定められた要件を土台とする。新たな要件はいずれも、複数の構成要素仕様を組み合わせて使用することに関するもの、または個々の構成要素仕様のいずれかにさらに制約を加えるものである。個々の構成要素仕様内の要件は本文書では繰り返さないため、それらの要件は各仕様を参照されたい。

contents.html: The scope of this document is limited to SCAP version 1.2. Other versions of SCAP and its component specifications, including emerging specifications, are not addressed here. Future versions of SCAP will be defined in distinct revisions of this document, each clearly labeled with a document revision number and the appropriate SCAP version number. SCAP revisions are managed through a coordinated process defined within the SCAP Release Cycle.6 The release cycle workflow manages changes related to SCAP specifications and validation processes including the addition of new specifications or updates to existing specifications. This process encourages community involvement, promotes transparency and awareness regarding proposed changes, and affords ample lead time to prepare for pending changes.

Combinations of these specifications can be used together for particular functions, such as security configuration checking. These functions, known as SCAP use cases, are ways in which a product can use SCAP. The collective XML content used for a use case is called an SCAP data stream, which is a specific instantiation of SCAP content. There are two types of SCAP data streams: an SCAP source data stream holds the input content, and an SCAP result data stream holds the output content. The major elements of a data stream, such as an XCCDF benchmark or a set of OVAL Definitions, are referred to as stream components.

contents.html: 3. SCAP Content Requirements and Recommendations

This section defines the SCAP 1.2 content syntax, structure, and development requirements and recommendations for SCAP-conformant content and products. Organizations are encouraged to adopt the optional recommendations to promote stronger interoperability and greater content consistency. The first part of the section discusses SCAP source data streams. The middle of the section groups requirements and recommendations by specification: XCCDF, OVAL, OCIL, CPE, CCE, CVE, CVSS, and CCSS, in that order. Finally, the last part of the section discusses applying XML digital signatures to source data streams.
contents.html_ja: 本節では、SCAP適合コンテンツおよび製品に対するSCAP 1.2コンテンツの構文、構造、開発に関する要件と推奨事項を定義する。相互運用性を高め、コンテンツの一貫性を向上させるため、組織には任意の推奨事項を採用することを推奨する。本節の前半ではSCAPソースデータストリームを扱う。中盤では仕様ごとに要件および推奨事項をまとめ、XCCDF、OVAL、OCIL、CPE、CCE、CVE、CVSS、CCSSの順に説明する。最後に、ソースデータストリームへのXMLデジタル署名の適用を扱う。

contents.html: 3.1 SCAP Source Data Stream
contents.html_ja: 3.1 SCAPソースデータストリーム

contents.html: This section discusses SCAP source data streams only; SCAP result data streams are discussed in Section 4.4 as part of the requirements for SCAP processing.

An SCAP source data stream collection is composed of SCAP data streams and SCAP source components. See http://scap.nist.gov/revision/1.2/#example for a sample of an SCAP source data stream collection and its sections. The components section contains an unbounded number of SCAP source components, each consisting of data expressed using one or more of the SCAP specifications. The data streams section contains one or more source data streams, each of which references the source components in the components section that compose the data stream. This model allows source components to be reused across multiple data streams. Many data streams are allowed in a data stream collection to allow grouping of related or similar source data streams. For example, NIST currently distributes the United States Government Configuration Baseline (USGCB)10 as a series of SCAP bundles. Source data streams that are similar or related (e.g., Microsoft Windows 7 content and Microsoft Windows 7 Firewall content) may be bundled into the same source data stream collection. Figure 1 shows the relationship between data stream collections, data streams, and components.

Each data stream is a collection of links to the components that they reference; each logical link encapsulates the information required to allow the content consumer to connect the components together within the data stream. Content authors MAY place components in any order. For example, some authors might choose to place dictionary components first to help optimize data stream parsing.

Links serve two purposes: to indicate which component is being referred to, and to provide a map to associate references within a component to other links within the data stream. The latter allows a data stream to define context for each component’s references within the bounds of the data stream’s own set of links. Figure 2 provides a conceptual example that illustrates how a data stream is constructed.

contents.html: The design of the SCAP source data stream is important for the following reasons:
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリームの設計が重要である理由は次のとおりである：

contents.html: Individual components may be developed outside of an SCAP data stream where the binding to other components is not necessarily known at the time the component is created.
contents.html_ja: 個々のコンポーネントは、作成時点では他のコンポーネントとの結び付きが判明していない場合があり、SCAPデータストリームの外部で開発できる。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream creates a binding between different components that were not necessarily designed to reference each other. For example, XCCDF was not designed to reference a particular checking system; it can reference OVAL, OCIL, and other checking systems.
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリームは、相互参照するよう設計されているとは限らない異なるコンポーネント間に結び付きを作る。例えば、XCCDFは特定の検査システムを参照するようには設計されていないが、OVAL、OCILなどの検査システムを参照できる。

contents.html: The logical link mapping in the data stream places a layer of capability within the data stream to control the dereferencing of URIs within components, creating a complete solution related to bundling components.
contents.html_ja: データストリーム内の論理リンクマッピングは、コンポーネント内のURI参照を解決するための機能層をデータストリームに設け、コンポーネントのバンドルに関する包括的な解決策を実現する。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream format will be useful in future communication models such as web services, transport protocols, tasking mechanisms, etc.
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリーム形式は、ウェブサービス、転送プロトコル、タスク管理機構など、将来の通信モデルで有用となる。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream format supports more comprehensive validation of component content, including interrelationships between components.
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリーム形式は、コンポーネント間の相互関係を含め、コンポーネントコンテンツのより包括的な検証を支援する。

contents.html: The SCAP source data stream collection SHALL validate against the XML schema representation for the source data stream, as well as all Schematron rules embedded within that schema. The SCAP components referenced by each <ds:component> and <ds:extended-component> element SHALL validate against the corresponding component schema and its embedded Schematron rules. All of the SCAP-related schemas are referenced at http://scap.nist.gov/revision/1.2/#schema. See Table 22 in Appendix C for a list of SCAP component schema and Schematron file locations. Each SCAP source data stream component SHALL use one of the elements specified in Table 12 as its document element. Each SCAP source data stream component SHOULD NOT use any constructs that are deprecated in its associated specification. While Section 4.1 requires that products support deprecated constructs, these constructs should be avoided to minimize the impact to content use when these constructs are removed from future revisions of the associated specifications. Any component in a data stream collection SHALL be referenced not more than once by any data stream in that collection. Table 12 - SCAP Source Data Stream Component Document Elements

contents.html: Schematron rules to check well-formed SCAP content. The Schematron files for the SCAP specification and its applicable component specifications are located at http://scap.nist.gov/revision/1.2/#schematron. Source content SHOULD pass all Schematron assertions in the Schematron rule files. When creating source content, failed assertions with a “warning” flag MAY be disregarded if the assertion discovers an issue in the content that is justifiable and expected based on the needs of the content author. When executing source content, all failed assertions with a “warning” flag MUST be disregarded.

contents.html: The Schematron rule sets are interpretations of the specifications, and the implementations of their rules are subject to change. Whenever a change is made to a Schematron file, the SCAP errata document will be updated and the new Schematron file will be posted. The latest Schematron file SHOULD be used in place of any earlier versions. If the latest file is unavailable, the version specified on the <ds:data-stream-collection> element’s @schematron-version attribute SHALL be used instead. Also, for the component specifications, the Schematron file on the SCAP website SHALL be used in place of any corresponding Schematron file available elsewhere. For example, a particular specification may have an official Schematron file available on a different website. In most cases, the copy on the SCAP website will be the same, but if issues in a Schematron file are discovered, the SCAP website may address these before the individual specification’s maintainers do.
contents.html_ja: Schematronルールセットは仕様の解釈であり、そのルールの実装は変更されることがある。Schematronファイルに変更が加えられるたびに、SCAP正誤表文書が更新され、新しいSchematronファイルが掲載される。以前のバージョンではなく、最新のSchematronファイルを使用すべきである（SHOULD）。最新のファイルが入手できない場合は、代わりに<ds:data-stream-collection>要素の@schematron-version属性で指定されたバージョンを使用するものとする（SHALL）。また、構成要素仕様については、他の場所で入手できる対応するSchematronファイルではなく、SCAPウェブサイト上のSchematronファイルを使用するものとする（SHALL）。たとえば、ある仕様の公式Schematronファイルが別のウェブサイトで入手できる場合がある。ほとんどの場合、SCAPウェブサイト上のコピーはそれと同一であるが、Schematronファイルに問題が見つかった場合、個々の仕様の保守者よりも先にSCAPウェブサイトが対処することがある。

contents.html: 3.2 Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF)
contents.html_ja: 3.2 拡張可能な構成チェックリスト記述形式（XCCDF）

contents.html: This section lists requirements and recommendations for using the Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) to express an XCCDF benchmark or tailoring component of an SCAP source data stream (see Table 12). They are organized by the following categories: general, <xccdf:Benchmark>, <xccdf:Profile>, <xccdf:Rule>, <xccdf:Value>, and <xccdf:Group>.
contents.html_ja: この節では、SCAPソースデータストリームのXCCDFベンチマークまたはテーラリングコンポーネントを表現するためにXCCDFを使用する際の要件と推奨事項を示す（表12を参照）。全般、<xccdf:Benchmark>、<xccdf:Profile>、<xccdf:Rule>、<xccdf:Value>、<xccdf:Group>に分類する。

contents.html: 3.2.1 General
The @xml:base attribute SHALL NOT be allowed in XCCDF content. This attribute is not compatible with the SCAP data stream model.

Descriptive information within XCCDF MAY be used by SCAP products to assist in the selection of the appropriate SCAP data stream, ensure that the most recent or correct version of an XCCDF document is used, and provide additional information about the document. The following requirements and conventions apply to the <xccdf:Benchmark>, <xccdf:Profile>, <xccdf:Value>, <xccdf:Group>, and <xccdf:Rule> elements:
One or more instances of the <xccdf:title> element SHALL be provided. Each instance MUST contain a text value that briefly indicates the purpose of the containing element.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:title>要素を一つ以上指定しなければならない（SHALL）。各要素には、包含要素の目的を簡潔に示すテキスト値を含めなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: One or more instances of the <xccdf:description> element SHALL be provided. Each instance MUST contain a text value that describes the purpose of the containing element.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:description>要素を一つ以上指定しなければならない（SHALL）。各要素には、包含要素の目的を説明するテキスト値を含めなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: XInclude elements SHALL NOT be included in XCCDF content [XINCLUDE].
All remaining OPTIONAL elements in the XCCDF schema MAY be included at the author’s discretion unless otherwise noted in this document.
3.2.2 The <xccdf:Benchmark> Element
contents.html_ja: 3.2.2 <xccdf:Benchmark>要素

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations apply to the <xccdf:Benchmark> element:
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:Benchmark>要素には次の要件および推奨事項が適用される。

contents.html: The <xccdf:version> element and the @id attribute SHALL be used together to uniquely identify all revisions of a benchmark. a. Multiple revisions of a single benchmark SHOULD have the same @id attribute value and different <xccdf:version> element values, so that someone who reviews the revisions can readily identify them as multiple versions of a single benchmark. b. Multiple revisions of a single benchmark SHOULD have <xccdf:version> element values that indicate the revision sequence, so that the history of changes from the original benchmark can be determined. c. The @time attribute of the <xccdf:version> element SHOULD be used for a timestamp of when the benchmark was defined.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:version>要素と@id属性は、ベンチマークのすべての改訂版を一意に識別するために併用しなければならない（SHALL）。a. 単一ベンチマークの複数の改訂版では、同じ@id属性値と異なる<xccdf:version>要素値を使用すべきである（SHOULD）。これにより、改訂版を確認する人が、単一ベンチマークの複数バージョンとして容易に識別できる。b. 単一ベンチマークの複数の改訂版では、元のベンチマークからの変更履歴を特定できるよう、改訂順序を示す<xccdf:version>要素値を使用すべきである（SHOULD）。c. ベンチマークが定義された日時のタイムスタンプには、<xccdf:version>要素の@time属性を使用すべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: The @update attribute of the <xccdf:version> element SHOULD be used for a URI that specifies where updates to the benchmark can be obtained.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:version>要素の@update属性は、ベンチマークの更新を入手できる場所を示すURIに使用すべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: The <xccdf:Benchmark> element SHALL have an @xml:lang attribute.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:Benchmark>要素は@xml:lang属性を持たなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: The @style attribute SHOULD have the value “SCAP_1.2”.
contents.html_ja: @style属性の値は“SCAP_1.2”とすべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: The <xccdf:status> element SHALL indicate the current status of the benchmark document. The associated text value SHALL be “draft” for documents released in public draft state and “accepted” for documents that have been officially released by an organization. The @date attribute SHALL be populated with the date of the status change. Additional <xccdf:status> elements MAY be included to indicate historic status transitions.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:status>要素は、ベンチマーク文書の現在の状態を示さなければならない（SHALL）。関連するテキスト値は、公開ドラフト状態で公開された文書では“draft”、組織が正式に公開した文書では“accepted”でなければならない（SHALL）。@date属性には状態変更の日付を設定しなければならない（SHALL）。過去の状態遷移を示すために、追加の<xccdf:status>要素を含めてもよい（MAY）。

contents.html: The <xccdf:metadata> element SHALL be provided and SHALL, at minimum, contain the Dublin Core [DCES] terms from Table 14. If provided, additional Dublin Core terms SHALL follow the required terms within the element sequence.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:metadata>要素を指定しなければならず（SHALL）、最低限、表14のDublin Core [DCES]用語を含めなければならない（SHALL）。追加のDublin Core用語を指定する場合、要素の並びでは必須用語の後に続けなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: 3.2.3 The <xccdf:Profile> Element
contents.html_ja: 3.2.3 <xccdf:Profile>要素

contents.html: As stated in the XCCDF specification, the use of an <xccdf:Profile> element is not required. SCAP content commonly includes <xccdf:Profile> elements, so people tend to assume that they are required, but they are optional.
Use of the <xccdf:set-complex-value> element within the <xccdf:Profile> element SHALL NOT be allowed.
3.2.4 The <xccdf:Rule> Element
contents.html_ja: 3.2.4 <xccdf:Rule>要素

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations apply to the <xccdf:Rule> element. The topics they address are <xccdf:ident> elements, <xccdf:check> elements, patches up-to-date rules, and CVSS and CCSS scores.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:Rule>要素には、次の要件および推奨事項が適用される。扱う項目は、<xccdf:ident>要素、<xccdf:check>要素、パッチ最新化ルール、CVSSおよびCCSSスコアである。

contents.html: 3.2.4.1 The <xccdf:ident> Element
contents.html_ja: 3.2.4.1 <xccdf:ident>要素

contents.html: Each <xccdf:Rule> element SHALL include an <xccdf:ident> element containing a CVE, CCE, or CPE identifier reference if an appropriate identifier exists. The meaning of the identifier MUST be consistent with the recommendation implemented by the <xccdf:Rule> element. If the rule references an OVAL Definition, then <xccdf:ident> element content SHALL match the corresponding CVE, CCE, or CPE identifier found in the associated OVAL Definition(s) if an appropriate identifier exists and if that OVAL Definition is the only input to the rule’s final result.

When referencing a CVE, CCE, or CPE identifier, an <xccdf:Rule> element MUST have a purpose consistent with one of the rows in Table 15. Based on the purpose of the <xccdf:Rule> element, the <xccdf:Rule> SHALL define its <xccdf:ident> element’s @system attribute using the corresponding value from Table 15. Also, if the <xccdf:Rule> element references an OVAL Definition, it SHALL reference an OVAL Definition of the specified class.

contents.html: Here is a partial example of a rule intended to check compliance with a configuration setting:
<xccdf:Rule id="xccdf_gov.nist.fdcc.xp_value_AuditAccountLogonEvents"> … <xccdf:ident system="http://cce.mitre.org">CCE-3867-0</xccdf:ident> … </xccdf:Rule>

See Section 4.5.1 for information on the meaning of a “pass/fail” rule result relating to each of the identifier types in Table 15. All rules that contain CCE, CPE, or CVE entries in their <xccdf:ident> elements MUST obey these meanings. As a result, such <xccdf:ident> elements MUST only be included either if the recommendation is identical to these associated meanings or if they have a @con:negate attribute (as described in Section 4.5.1) set to comply with the intended meaning (by default, @con:negate is set to false). In SCAP, an <xccdf:ident> element is not simply a reference to related material – it is a declaration of exact alignment with the described meanings.

An <xccdf:ident> element referencing a CVE, CCE, or CPE identifier SHALL be ordered before other <xccdf:ident> elements referencing non-SCAP identifiers. Identifiers from previous revisions of CCE or CPE MAY also be specified following the SCAP identifiers.
3.2.4.2 The <xccdf:check> Element
contents.html_ja: 3.2.4.2 <xccdf:check>要素

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations apply to the <xccdf:check> element:
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:check>要素には、次の要件および推奨事項が適用される：

contents.html: The <xccdf:check-content> element SHALL NOT be used to embed check content directly into XCCDF content.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:check-content>要素を使用して、チェックコンテンツをXCCDFコンテンツに直接埋め込んではならない（SHALL NOT）。

contents.html: At least one <xccdf:check-content-ref> element MUST be provided for each <xccdf:check> element.
contents.html_ja: 各<xccdf:check>要素には、少なくとも一つの<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素を指定しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: When evaluating an <xccdf:check-content-ref> element within an <xccdf:check> element, its @href attribute either MUST contain a “#” + @id of a <ds:component-ref> element or MUST be resolved in the context of the XML Catalog specified as part of the <ds:component-ref> element that is referencing this benchmark. In either case, the @href attribute MUST ultimately resolve to a <ds:component-ref> element in the data stream referencing the benchmark containing this <xccdf:check-content-ref> element. See Section 3.1.1 for additional information on <ds:component-ref> resolution.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:check>要素内の<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素を評価する際、その@href属性には、“#” + <ds:component-ref>要素の@idを含めるか（MUST）、またはこのベンチマークを参照する<ds:component-ref>要素に関連付けられたXML Catalogのコンテキスト内で解決しなければならない（MUST）。いずれの場合も、@href属性は最終的に、この<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素を含むベンチマークを参照するデータストリーム内の<ds:component-ref>要素に解決されなければならない（MUST）。<ds:component-ref>の解決に関する追加情報は第3.1.1節を参照。

contents.html: This version of SCAP supports the OVAL and OCIL check systems. Use of these check systems SHALL be restricted as follows:
contents.html_ja: このバージョンのSCAPはOVALおよびOCILチェックシステムをサポートする。これらのチェックシステムの使用は、次のとおり制限されなければならない（SHALL）：

contents.html: 1. OVAL check system
i. Use of the OVAL check system SHALL be indicated by setting the <xccdf:check> element’s @system attribute to “http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5 ”.
ii. The @href attribute in the <xccdf:check-content-ref> element MUST reference an OVAL source data stream component using the <ds:component-ref> approach defined above.

iii. Use of the @name attribute in the <xccdf:check-content-ref> element is OPTIONAL. If present, it MUST reference an OVAL Definition in the designated OVAL source data stream component, otherwise see Section 4.5.2 for information on use of the @multi-check attribute.
2. OCIL check system
i. OCIL questionnaires SHOULD NOT be used if OVAL can perform the same check correctly.
ii. Use of the OCIL check system SHALL be indicated by setting the <xccdf:check> element’s @system attribute to “http://scap.nist.gov/schema/ocil/2”.
iii. The @href attribute in the <xccdf:check-content-ref> element MUST reference an OCIL source data stream component using the <ds:component-ref> approach defined above.

iv. Use of the @name attribute in the <xccdf:check-content-ref> element is OPTIONAL. If present, it MUST reference an OCIL questionnaire in the designated OCIL source data stream component, otherwise see Section 4.5.2 for information on use of the @multi-check attribute.
v. Follow the additional requirements in Appendix B of NIST Interagency Report (IR) 7692, Specifications for the Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL) Version 2.0 [OCIL].
If a check system that is not supported by SCAP is used in XCCDF content, this content SHALL NOT be considered well-formed with regards to SCAP.
contents.html_ja:
iv. <xccdf:check-content-ref>要素における@name属性の使用は OPTIONAL である。存在する場合、それは指定されたOCILソースデータストリームコンポーネント内のOCIL質問票を参照しなければならない（MUST）。存在しない場合は、@multi-check属性の使用について第4.5.2節を参照のこと。
v. NIST Interagency Report（IR）7692、Specifications for the Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL) Version 2.0 [OCIL]の付録Bにある追加要件に従う。

contents.html: 3.2.4.3 Use of a Patches Up-To-Date Rule
contents.html_ja: 3.2.4.3 パッチ最新化ルールの使用

contents.html: An OVAL source data stream component MAY be used to represent a series of checks to verify that patches have been installed. Historically, an XCCDF convention has been used to identify such a reference. An XCCDF benchmark MAY include a patches up-to-date rule that MUST reference an OVAL source data stream component. When implementing a patches up-to-date XCCDF rule, the following approach SHALL be used:
contents.html_ja: パッチがインストール済みであることを確認する一連のチェックを表すために、OVALソースデータストリームコンポーネントを使用してもよい（MAY）。このような参照の識別には、従来XCCDFの規約が使用されてきた。XCCDFベンチマークには、OVALソースデータストリームコンポーネントを参照しなければならない（MUST）パッチ最新化ルールを含めてもよい（MAY）。パッチ最新化XCCDFルールを実装する際は、次の方法を使用しなければならない（SHALL）：

contents.html: The source data stream MUST include the OVAL source data stream component referenced by the patches up-to-date rule, which contains one or more OVAL patch class definitions.
contents.html_ja: ソースデータストリームには、パッチ最新化ルールが参照するOVALソースデータストリームコンポーネントを含めなければならない（MUST）。そのコンポーネントには、一つ以上のOVALパッチクラス定義が含まれる。

contents.html: The <xccdf:Rule> element that references an OVAL source data stream component SHALL have the @id attribute value of “xccdf_NAMESPACE_rule_security_patches_up_to_date”, where NAMESPACE is the reverse DNS format namespace associated with the content maintainer.
contents.html_ja: OVALソースデータストリームコンポーネントを参照する<xccdf:Rule>要素は、“xccdf_NAMESPACE_rule_security_patches_up_to_date”という@id属性値を持たなければならない（SHALL）。ここでNAMESPACEはコンテンツ保守担当者に関連付けられた逆引きDNS形式のnamespaceである。

contents.html: Each <xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL omit the @name attribute.
contents.html_ja: 各<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素では@name属性を省略しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: The @multi-check attribute of the <xccdf:check> element SHOULD be set to “true”. This causes a separate <xccdf:rule-result> to be generated for each OVAL Definition. See Section 4.5.2 for more information.
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:check>要素の@multi-check属性は“true”に設定すべきである（SHOULD）。これにより、OVAL定義ごとに個別の<xccdf:rule-result>が生成される。詳細は第4.5.2節を参照。

contents.html: Here is a patches up-to-date rule example:
contents.html_ja: パッチ最新化ルールの例：

contents.html: <xccdf:Rule id="xccdf_gov.nist.fdcc.xp_rule_security_patches_up_to_date" selected="true"> <xccdf:title>Security Patches Up-To-Date</xccdf:title> <xccdf:description>Keep systems up to current patch levels </xccdf:description> <xccdf:check system="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5" multi-check="true"> <xccdf:check-content-ref href="scap-win2000-patches.xml"/> </xccdf:check> </xccdf:Rule>
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:Rule id="xccdf_gov.nist.fdcc.xp_rule_security_patches_up_to_date" selected="true"> <xccdf:title>Security Patches Up-To-Date</xccdf:title> <xccdf:description>Keep systems up to current patch levels </xccdf:description> <xccdf:check system="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5" multi-check="true"> <xccdf:check-content-ref href="scap-win2000-patches.xml"/> </xccdf:check> </xccdf:Rule>

contents.html: 3.2.4.4 CVSS and CCSS Scores
contents.html_ja: 3.2.4.4 CVSSおよびCCSSスコア

contents.html: SCAP 1.0 required the inclusion of static CVSS scores in XCCDF vulnerability-related rules. However, CVSS base scores sometimes change over time, such as when more information is available about a particular vulnerability, and CVSS temporal and environmental scores are intended to change to reflect current threats, security controls, and other factors. During scoring, current CVSS scores acquired dynamically, such as from a data feed, SHOULD be used in place of the @weight attribute within XCCDF vulnerability-related rules. Section 3.8 contains additional requirements for CVSS usage.

CCSS scores are more stable than CVSS scores, but they still may change over time. While the default version14 of OVAL used in SCAP 1.2 SHALL be OVAL version 5.10, SCAP content SHOULD utilize the earliest SCAP-supported version of OVAL that includes all required tests and is necessary to properly address the SCAP content’s purpose or use case. contents.html: This section lists recommendations for using the Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL) to express an OCIL component of an SCAP source data stream (see Table 12).

OCIL content SHOULD be used for checking rules that cannot be fully automated with OVAL. For example, a particular software product may not have an application programming interface (API) that supports OVAL use. Another example is performing a check that requires user interaction, such as asking the user to look up information within a management console or to report a serial number affixed to a computing device. OCIL can also be used to collect a user’s own information, such as whether the user participated in a recent security training session.

If an <ocil:questionnaire> element maps to one or more CCE, CVE, and/or CPE identifiers, it SHOULD include <ocil:reference> elements that reference those identifiers using the corresponding following format:
<ocil:reference href="http://cce.mitre.org">CCE_identifier</ocil:reference>

<ocil:reference href="http://cpe.mitre.org">CPE_identifier</ocil:reference>
3.5 Common Platform Enumeration (CPE)
contents.html_ja: 3.5 Common Platform Enumeration（CPE）

contents.html: This section lists requirements and recommendations for using Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) to express a CPE component of an SCAP source data stream (see Table 12).

The Official CPE Dictionary data feed15 MAY be used by SCAP components to reference CPE names. If use of the Official CPE Dictionary is impractical, a subset of the dictionary MAY be used instead. Creating the reduced official dictionary involves first identifying every CPE in <xccdf:platform> and <cpe2:fact-ref> elements contained within referenced <cpe2:platform-specification> elements in every benchmark in the data stream. Then these CPEs MUST be matched against every entry in the Official CPE Dictionary using the CPE name matching algorithm [CPE-M]. All CPEs matched in the official dictionary with a result of EQUAL or SUPERSET MUST be included in the reduced official dictionary.

One or more third-party dictionaries MAY be included in a data stream as well. All such third-party dictionaries SHOULD follow the requirements of the CPE Dictionary specification [CPE-D]. If including an entire third-party dictionary is impractical, a subset of the dictionary MAY be used instead. The reduced dictionary MUST be created using the same procedure outlined for creating a subset of the official dictionary.
In all cases, a dictionary component MAY be remote to the data stream collection.

Each CPE name [CPE-N] in an <xccdf:platform> or <cpe2:fact-ref> element within an XCCDF document SHALL match at least one CPE entry in a dictionary referenced by the data stream. A match is considered an EQUAL or SUPERSET result when matching the CPE name to a dictionary entry, as defined in the CPE Name Matching specification [CPE-M]. Only non-deprecated names SHOULD be used.

Checklist authors SHOULD ensure that each CPE name [CPE-N] they specify in an <xccdf:platform> or <cpe2:fact-ref> element within an XCCDF document has a check associated with its CPE name. If a corresponding check does not exist, then it will not be possible to fully detect the presence of the product and determine platform applicability. Because there may be a lag between the time that a new product is available and the Official CPE Dictionary is updated to include a CPE name for that product, third-party dictionaries would need to be used to compensate for the lag.

[CPE-D] provides the defining structure of a CPE dictionary. A <cpe2_dict:cpe-item> element MAY contain one or more <cpe2-dict:check> elements that reference OVAL inventory class definitions using the following format: <cpe2_dict:check system="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5" [href="oval_URL"]>oval_inventory_definition_id</cpe2_dict:check>
15 The Official CPE Dictionary is located at http://nvd.nist.gov/cpe.cfm.

contents.html: 3.6 Common Configuration Enumeration (CCE)
contents.html_ja: 3.6 Common Configuration Enumeration（CCE）

contents.html: To maintain consistency and accuracy, SCAP content referencing a configuration setting SHALL use the official CCE identifier if a CCE entry for a particular configuration setting exists in the official CCE list. If no CCE entry exists for the configuration setting of interest, the content author SHOULD seek to have a CCE identifier issued for the configuration setting. See the OVAL compliance class definition requirements in Section 3.3 and the <xccdf:ident> requirements in Section 3.2.4.1 for additional requirements involving CCE identifier references.
contents.html_ja: 一貫性と正確性を維持するため、設定項目を参照するSCAPコンテンツは、その設定項目のCCEエントリが公式CCEリストに存在する場合、公式のCCE識別子を使用するものとする（SHALL）。対象とする設定項目のCCEエントリが存在しない場合、コンテンツ作成者は、その設定項目にCCE識別子が発行されるよう求めるべきである（SHOULD）。CCE識別子の参照に関するその他の要件については、Section 3.3のOVALコンプライアンスクラス定義の要件と、Section 3.2.4.1の<xccdf:ident>の要件を参照されたい。

contents.html: The current official CCE list is available at http://cce.mitre.org/lists/cce_list.html and new CCEs can be requested from the CCE Content Team. Submitters should review the information provided at http://cce.mitre.org/lists/creation_process.html regarding CCE core concepts and design constraints before submitting proposals for new CCE entries. Use of an official, dynamic data feed is preferred to static coding of CCE-related supporting information in SCAP data sources. For example, NVD provides a data feed16 that is the authoritative mapping between CCE identifiers and the control identifiers defined in NIST SP 800-53. Embedding control identifiers within SCAP content is strongly discouraged due to the maintenance burden that it imposes on content maintainers when the control identifiers are revised. A preferred technique is to embed only the CCE identifiers within SCAP content; when mappings to NIST SP 800-53 control identifiers are needed, dynamically acquire them from the official data feed and associate them to the SCAP content based on its embedded CCE identifiers.

contents.html: 3.7 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)
contents.html_ja: 3.7 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures（CVE）

contents.html: CVE references in SCAP content MAY include both “candidate” and “entry” status identifiers. Deprecated CVE identifiers SHALL NOT be used.
contents.html_ja: SCAPコンテンツ内のCVE参照には、「candidate」と「entry」の両方の状態の識別子を含めてもよい（MAY）。廃止されたCVE識別子は使用しないものとする（SHALL NOT）。

contents.html: If a CVE identifier exists for a particular vulnerability, the official CVE identifier SHALL be used. If no CVE exists for the software flaw, an alternate identifier MAY be used, but the user SHOULD seek to have a CVE identifier issued for the vulnerability. The process for submitting unpublished vulnerabilities and obtaining CVE identifiers is available at http://cve.mitre.org/cve/obtain_id.html.
contents.html_ja: 特定の脆弱性についてCVE識別子が存在する場合は、公式のCVE識別子を使用するものとする（SHALL）。そのソフトウェアの欠陥についてCVEが存在しない場合は、代替の識別子を使用してもよい（MAY）が、利用者はその脆弱性にCVE識別子が発行されるよう求めるべきである（SHOULD）。未公開の脆弱性を提出し、CVE識別子を取得するためのプロセスは http://cve.mitre.org/cve/obtain_id.html で入手できる。

contents.html: NIST provides a CVE data feed to support dynamic and current vulnerability information and associated metadata (e.g., CVSS values). The current schema is available at http://nvd.nist.gov/download.cfm.
contents.html_ja: NISTは、動的かつ最新の脆弱性情報と関連するメタデータ（例：CVSS値）を支援するため、CVEデータフィードを提供している。現在のスキーマは http://nvd.nist.gov/download.cfm で入手できる。

contents.html: 3.8 Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS)
contents.html_ja: 3.8 Common Vulnerability Scoring System（CVSS）

contents.html: The NIST CVE data feed, discussed in Section 3.7, is one source of CVSS base score and vector data that MAY be used by products to support additional use cases built on SCAP usage. In support of these additional use cases, CVSS base scores and vectors from this data feed MAY be used by products along with temporal and environmental scores and vectors from other sources.
contents.html_ja: 第3.7節で説明したNIST CVEデータフィードは、SCAP利用を基盤とする追加ユースケースを支援するために製品が使用してもよい（MAY）CVSS基本スコアおよびベクトルの一つの情報源である。これらの追加ユースケースを支援するため、このデータフィードのCVSS基本スコアおよびベクトルを、他の情報源の時間的スコアおよび環境スコア、ならびにベクトルとともに製品が使用してもよい（MAY）。

contents.html: 3.9 Common Configuration Scoring System (CCSS)
contents.html_ja: 3.9 Common Configuration Scoring System（CCSS）

contents.html: CCSS base, temporal, and environmental scores and vectors MAY be used by products. Adopters of CCSS should be aware that it has significant differences from CVSS. Unlike CVSS data, which can be used by itself to aid in prioritizing vulnerability remediation efforts, CCSS data is not directly useful in the same way. Instead, CCSS data needs to be considered in the context of each organization’s security policies and in the context of dependencies among vulnerabilities. See [CCSS] for additional information.
contents.html_ja: CCSSの基本スコア、時間的スコア、環境スコアおよびベクトルは製品が使用してもよい（MAY）。CCSSの採用者は、CCSSがCVSSと大きく異なる点に留意すべきである。脆弱性修正作業の優先順位付けを支援するため単独で使用できるCVSSデータとは異なり、CCSSデータは同じ方法では直接役立たない。CCSSデータは、各組織のセキュリティポリシーと、脆弱性間の依存関係を踏まえて検討する必要がある。詳細は[CCSS]を参照。

contents.html: 3.10 XML Digital Signature
contents.html_ja: 3.10 XML電子署名

contents.html: Digitally signing source data streams is important to ensuring the integrity and trustworthiness of legitimate content, while preventing rogue content from being executed. Leveraging the Trust Model for Security Automation Data (TMSAD) specification [TMSAD] for SCAP can improve the legitimacy of authoritative content and create a more secure environment. As such, content authors MAY digitally sign source content following the guidelines in [TMSAD], along with the following requirements.
contents.html_ja: ソースデータストリームにデジタル署名することは、正当なコンテンツの完全性と信頼性を確保し、不正なコンテンツの実行を防ぐうえで重要である。SCAPにTrust Model for Security Automation Data（TMSAD）仕様[TMSAD]を活用することで、正式なコンテンツの正当性を高め、より安全な環境を構築できる。そのため、コンテンツ作成者は、[TMSAD]のガイドラインと以下の要件に従ってソースコンテンツにデジタル署名してもよい（MAY）。

contents.html: One or more XML digital signatures MAY be included as the last elements in the SCAP source data stream collection root element. Each signature MUST be represented as a <dsig:Signature> element and follow the W3C recommendation [DSIG]. Each <dsig:Signature> element MUST sign only one data stream.
contents.html_ja: SCAPソースデータストリームコレクションのルート要素の最後の要素として、1つ以上のXMLデジタル署名を含めてもよい（MAY）。各署名は<dsig:Signature>要素として表現し、W3C勧告[DSIG]に従わなければならない（MUST）。各<dsig:Signature>要素は、1つのデータストリームのみに署名しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: 16 http://nvd.nist.gov/cce.cfm
contents.html_ja: 16 http://nvd.nist.gov/cce.cfm

contents.html: The <dsig:Signature> element MUST follow the recommendations in [TMSAD] and these additional requirements:
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Signature>要素は、[TMSAD]の推奨事項と以下の追加要件に従わなければならない（MUST）：

contents.html: A <dsig:Manifest> element MUST be included within the <dsig:Signature> element as a <dsig:Object> element. The <dsig:Manifest> element MUST have a <dsig:Reference> element for each local component referenced by the data stream being signed. External components MAY be omitted from the <dsig:Manifest> element. Each <dsig:Reference> element referencing a <ds:component> or <ds:extended-component> element MUST point to the component being signed by identifying the component in the @URI attribute using “#” + @Id of the component.
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Manifest>要素は、<dsig:Object>要素として<dsig:Signature>要素内に含まれなければならない（MUST）。<dsig:Manifest>要素には、署名対象のデータストリームが参照する各ローカルコンポーネントに対する<dsig:Reference>要素を含めなければならない（MUST）。外部コンポーネントは<dsig:Manifest>要素から省略してもよい（MAY）。<ds:component>要素または<ds:extended-component>要素を参照する各<dsig:Reference>要素は、@URI属性に“#” + コンポーネントの@Idを指定して、署名対象コンポーネントを指さなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: A <dsig:SignatureProperties> element MUST be included within the <dsig:Signature> element as a <dsig:Object> element. At least one <dsig:SignatureProperty> element MUST be populated with <dt:signature-info> as specified in [TMSAD].
contents.html_ja: <dsig:SignatureProperties>要素は、<dsig:Object>要素として<dsig:Signature>要素内に含まれなければならない（MUST）。少なくとも一つの<dsig:SignatureProperty>要素に、[TMSAD]で指定された<dt:signature-info>を設定しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: The first <dsig:Reference> element in a <dsig:Signature> element MUST be to the <ds:data-stream> element being signed. The <ds:data-stream> element MUST be referenced in the @URI attribute using “#” + @Id of the <ds:data-stream> element.
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Signature>要素内の最初の<dsig:Reference>要素は、署名対象の<ds:data-stream>要素を参照しなければならない（MUST）。<ds:data-stream>要素は、“#” + <ds:data-stream>要素の@Idを用いて@URI属性内で参照しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: The second <dsig:Reference> element in a <dsig:Signature> element MUST be to the <dsig:SignatureProperties> element captured in a <dsig:Object> element within the <dsig:Signature> element. The <dsig:SignatureProperties> element MUST be referenced in the @URI attribute using “#” + @Id of the<dsig:SignatureProperties> element.
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Signature>要素内の第二の<dsig:Reference>要素は、<dsig:Signature>要素内の<dsig:Object>要素に格納された<dsig:SignatureProperties>要素を参照しなければならない（MUST）。<dsig:SignatureProperties>要素は、“#” + <dsig:SignatureProperties>要素の@Idを用いて@URI属性内で参照しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: The third <dsig:Reference> element MUST be to the <dsig:Manifest> element captured in a <dsig:Object> element with the <dsig:Signature> element. The <dsig:Manifest> element MUST be referenced in the @URI attribute using “#” + @Id attribute of the <dsig:Manifest> element.
contents.html_ja: 第三の<dsig:Reference>要素は、<dsig:Signature>要素内の<dsig:Object>要素に格納された<dsig:Manifest>要素を参照しなければならない（MUST）。<dsig:Manifest>要素は、“#” + <dsig:Manifest>要素の@Id属性を用いて@URI属性内で参照しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: <dsig:Reference> elements on the <dsig:Manifest> element SHOULD be in the same order as the <ds:component-ref> elements on the data stream being signed.
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Manifest>要素内の<dsig:Reference>要素は、署名対象のデータストリーム上の<ds:component-ref>要素と同じ順序で並べるべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: Key information SHOULD be provided on the <dsig:Signature> element.
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Signature>要素に鍵情報を指定すべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: 4. SCAP Content Processing Requirements and Recommendations
contents.html_ja: 4. SCAPコンテンツの処理に関する要件と推奨事項

contents.html: This section defines the processing requirements that SCAP content consumers MUST follow in order to correctly process SCAP 1.2 content. This section also provides recommendations that are not mandatory; organizations are encouraged to adopt them to promote stronger interoperability and greater consistency. The topics covered in the first part of this section are legacy support, source data streams, and XCCDF processing. The end of the section covers result-related topics: SCAP result data streams, XCCDF results, OVAL results, OCIL results, and result data stream signing.
contents.html_ja: この節では、SCAP 1.2コンテンツを正しく処理するために、SCAPコンテンツ利用者が従わなければならない（MUST）処理要件を定義する。また、必須ではない推奨事項も示す。相互運用性の向上と一貫性の強化を促すため、組織にはこれらを採用することを推奨する。節の前半では、レガシーサポート、ソースデータストリーム、XCCDF処理を扱う。後半では結果関連のトピック、すなわちSCAP結果データストリーム、XCCDF結果、OVAL結果、OCIL結果、結果データストリームの署名を扱う。

contents.html: 4.1 Legacy Support
contents.html_ja: 4.1 レガシーサポート

contents.html: Content consumers supporting SCAP 1.2 SHALL process SCAP 1.2 content and SCAP 1.0 content. Content consumers SHALL process SCAP content as defined under the corresponding version of NIST SP 800-126 (for SCAP 1.2, this revision; for SCAP 1.0, the original release).17 Content consumers that process legacy SCAP content MUST be capable of outputting results in the same SCAP version as the source content, and MAY convert the legacy SCAP results into SCAP 1.2 results.
contents.html_ja: SCAP 1.2をサポートするコンテンツ利用者は、SCAP 1.2コンテンツとSCAP 1.0コンテンツを処理するものとする（SHALL）。コンテンツ利用者は、対応するバージョンのNIST SP 800-126（SCAP 1.2の場合は本改訂版、SCAP 1.0の場合は初版）で定義されたとおりにSCAPコンテンツを処理するものとする（SHALL）。17 レガシーSCAPコンテンツを処理するコンテンツ利用者は、ソースコンテンツと同じSCAPバージョンで結果を出力できなければならず（MUST）、レガシーSCAPの結果をSCAP 1.2の結果に変換してもよい（MAY）。

contents.html: Within the SCAP component specifications, certain constructs may be deprecated.18 SCAP content consumers MUST support all deprecated constructs because they are still valid. This requirement ensures that legacy content that made use of these deprecated constructs continues to be supported.
contents.html_ja: SCAP構成要素仕様の中では、特定の構文が廃止予定とされている場合がある。18 SCAPコンテンツ利用者は、廃止予定の構文もすべて依然として有効であるため、それらをすべてサポートしなければならない（MUST）。この要件により、これらの廃止予定の構文を使用したレガシーコンテンツが引き続きサポートされることが保証される。

contents.html: Content consumers supporting OVAL SHALL support OVAL Definition documents written against OVAL versions 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9, and 5.10.
contents.html_ja: OVALをサポートするコンテンツ利用者は、OVALバージョン5.3、5.4、5.5、5.6、5.7、5.8、5.9、5.10に準拠して記述されたOVAL Definition文書をサポートするものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: 4.2 Source Data Streams
contents.html_ja: 4.2 ソースデータストリーム

contents.html: Content consumers SHALL be capable of validating SCAP content against the appropriate schemas and Schematron stylesheets, detecting and reporting errors, and failing gracefully if there are errors. The relevant XML schemas are located at http://scap.nist.gov/revision/1.2/#schema, and the relevant Schematron rule sets at http://scap.nist.gov/revision/1.2/#schematron. See Section 3.1 for additional information on the Schematron rule sets.
contents.html_ja: コンテンツ利用者は、適切なスキーマとSchematronスタイルシートに照らしてSCAPコンテンツを検証し、エラーを検出・報告し、エラーがある場合には適切に失敗する能力を備えるものとする（SHALL）。関連するXMLスキーマは http://scap.nist.gov/revision/1.2/#schema に、関連するSchematronルールセットは http://scap.nist.gov/revision/1.2/#schematron にある。Schematronルールセットに関する追加情報はSection 3.1を参照されたい。

contents.html: Content consumers SHOULD validate XML digital signatures if they exist in the content. Validating a signature includes confirming that the signature value is valid, all of the reference hashes in the signature and manifest are correct, and the public key used to verify the signature is from a trusted source. A data stream with a signature that does not validate SHOULD NOT be evaluated by a content consumer.
contents.html_ja: コンテンツ利用者は、コンテンツ内にXMLデジタル署名が存在する場合、それを検証すべきである（SHOULD）。署名の検証には、署名値が有効であること、署名およびマニフェスト内のすべての参照ハッシュが正しいこと、署名の検証に使用する公開鍵が信頼できる発行元のものであることの確認が含まれる。検証に失敗する署名を持つデータストリームは、コンテンツ利用者が評価すべきではない（SHOULD NOT）。

contents.html: Whenever a <ds:extended-component> that is not recognized by the tool is referenced from a <ds:data-stream>, <ds:component>, or <ds:extended-component> element, the tool SHALL issue a warning.
contents.html_ja: ツールが認識しない<ds:extended-component>が<ds:data-stream>、<ds:component>、または<ds:extended-component>要素から参照されている場合、そのツールは警告を発するものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: If more than one <ds:data-stream> element is specified on the <ds:data-stream-collection>, the ID of the <ds:data-stream> to execute MUST be indicated to the content consumer, and the content consumer MUST use the specified <ds:data-stream>. If more than one <xccdf:Benchmark> is referenced by a <ds:data-stream>, the ID of the <xccdf:Benchmark> to execute MUST be indicated to the content consumer, and the content consumer MUST process the indicated <xccdf:Benchmark>. Because SCAP and its component specifications do not formally define how to designate a particular data stream, benchmark, etc. in these cases, it is expected that products will implement these capabilities in a proprietary way.
contents.html_ja: <ds:data-stream-collection>に複数の<ds:data-stream>要素が指定されている場合、実行する<ds:data-stream>のIDをコンテンツ利用者に示さなければならず（MUST）、コンテンツ利用者は指定された<ds:data-stream>を使用しなければならない（MUST）。1つの<ds:data-stream>から複数の<xccdf:Benchmark>が参照されている場合、実行する<xccdf:Benchmark>のIDをコンテンツ利用者に示さなければならず（MUST）、コンテンツ利用者は示された<xccdf:Benchmark>を処理しなければならない（MUST）。SCAPとその構成要素仕様は、これらの場合に特定のデータストリームやベンチマークなどを指定する方法を正式には定義していないため、製品はこれらの機能を独自の方法で実装することが想定される。

contents.html: 17 http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/PubsSPs.html#800-126
contents.html_ja: 17 http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/PubsSPs.html#800-126

contents.html: 18 The OVAL Language Deprecation policy is available here: http://oval.mitre.org/language/about/deprecation.html
contents.html_ja: 18 OVAL言語の廃止予定ポリシーは、http://oval.mitre.org/language/about/deprecation.html で入手できる。

contents.html: 4.3 XCCDF Processing
contents.html_ja: 4.3 XCCDF処理

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations pertain to content consumers processing XCCDF benchmark and tailoring components from an SCAP source data stream.
contents.html_ja: この節の要件および推奨事項は、SCAPソースデータストリームからXCCDFベンチマークおよびテーラリングコンポーネントを処理するコンテンツ利用者に適用される。

contents.html: 4.3.1 CPE Applicability Processing
contents.html_ja: 4.3.1 CPE適用可能性の処理

contents.html: CPEs referenced in an <xccdf:platform> element directly or by a <cpe2:fact-ref> contained within a referenced <cpe2:platform-specification> element SHALL be evaluated as follows to determine their presence on a machine:
contents.html_ja: <xccdf:platform>要素内で直接参照されるCPE、および参照先の<cpe2:platform-specification>要素内に含まれる<cpe2:fact-ref>を介して参照されるCPEは、マシン上での存在を判断するため、次のとおり評価しなければならない（SHALL）：

contents.html: The CPE SHALL be matched against all CPEs in all of the dictionaries referenced by the <ds:data-stream> element. All CPEs that return an EQUAL or SUPERSET result as defined in CPE Name Matching [CPE-M] SHALL be used in evaluating the <xccdf:platform> or <cpe2:fact-ref>.
contents.html_ja: CPEは、<ds:data-stream>要素が参照するすべての辞書に含まれるすべてのCPEと照合しなければならない（SHALL）。CPE名照合[CPE-M]で定義されるEQUALまたはSUPERSETの結果となるCPEはすべて、<xccdf:platform>または<cpe2:fact-ref>の評価に使用しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: Either a list of CPEs found on the target asset MUST be known before the scan, or a list SHALL be generated. If a previously known list is used, it MUST be equivalent to a newly generated list. To generate the list, the <cpe2_dict:check> element data associated with the found <cpe2_dict:cpe-item> elements SHALL be evaluated against the target using the referenced OVAL inventory class definition. If a <cpe2_dict:check> returns “pass”, then the corresponding CPE SHALL be added to the list of CPEs found on the target.
contents.html_ja: 対象資産上で見つかったCPEの一覧をスキャン前に把握しておかなければならない（MUST）、または一覧を生成しなければならない（SHALL）。以前に把握した一覧を使用する場合、新たに生成した一覧と同等でなければならない（MUST）。一覧を生成するには、見つかった<cpe2_dict:cpe-item>要素に関連付けられた<cpe2_dict:check>要素のデータを、参照されたOVALインベントリクラス定義を用いて対象に対して評価しなければならない（SHALL）。<cpe2_dict:check>の結果が“pass”であれば、対応するCPEを対象上で見つかったCPEの一覧に追加しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: The list of CPEs found on the target asset, along with the <xccdf:platform> or <cpe2:platform-specification> SHALL be used as input to the CPE Applicability Language [CPE-L] algorithm to determine the XCCDF Benchmark applicability to the target asset.
contents.html_ja: 対象資産上で見つかったCPEの一覧と<xccdf:platform>または<cpe2:platform-specification>は、対象資産に対するXCCDFベンチマークの適用可否を判断するため、CPE Applicability Language [CPE-L]アルゴリズムへの入力として使用しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: 4.3.2 Check System Usage
contents.html_ja: 4.3.2 チェックシステムの使用

contents.html: If an XCCDF component has multiple <xccdf:check-content-ref> elements, then check processing SHALL be performed according to [XCCDF:7.2.3.5.1] with the following changes:
contents.html_ja: XCCDFコンポーネントに複数の<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素がある場合、次の変更を加えたうえで[XCCDF:7.2.3.5.1]に従ってチェック処理を実行しなければならない（SHALL）：

contents.html: For each <xccdf:check-content-ref> element, a content consumer either MUST attempt to retrieve the document referenced by the <ds:component-ref> element that is referenced directly by the <xccdf:check-content-ref> element’s @href attribute, or it MUST resolve the @href attribute within the context of the XML Catalog specified as part of the <ds:component-ref> element used to reference this benchmark. If not resolvable, the next available <xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL be evaluated. If none of the <xccdf:check-content-ref> elements are resolvable, then the result of the rule evaluation SHALL be the XCCDF “notchecked” status and processing of the check SHALL end.
contents.html_ja: 各<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素について、コンテンツ利用者は、同要素の@href属性が直接参照する<ds:component-ref>要素が参照する文書の取得を試みるか（MUST）、またはこのベンチマークの参照に用いる<ds:component-ref>要素の一部として指定されたXML Catalogのコンテキスト内で@href属性を解決しなければならない（MUST）。解決できない場合は、次に利用可能な<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素を評価しなければならない（SHALL）。どの<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素も解決できない場合、ルール評価の結果はXCCDFの“notchecked”状態でなければならず（SHALL）、チェック処理を終了しなければならない（SHALL）。

contents.html: Once a resolvable <xccdf:check-content-ref> element is found, then check system processing SHALL proceed. When evaluating a rule, an <xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:message> with the @severity attribute value of “info” SHALL be generated, indicating the <xccdf:check-content-ref> @href attribute and @name attribute, if provided.
contents.html_ja: 解決可能な<xccdf:check-content-ref>要素が見つかったら、チェックシステム処理を続行しなければならない（SHALL）。ルールの評価時には、@severity属性値を“info”とする<xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:message>を生成しなければならない（SHALL）。このメッセージには、<xccdf:check-content-ref>の@href属性、および指定されている場合は@name属性を示す。

contents.html: Content consumers SHALL implement check systems supported by SCAP as defined in Section 3.2.4.2. Content consumers MAY implement check systems that are not supported by SCAP. If a tool encounters a check system it does not support, it MUST issue a warning and it MUST continue processing according to the [XCCDF] specification.
contents.html_ja: コンテンツ利用者は、第3.2.4.2節で定義される、SCAPがサポートするチェックシステムを実装しなければならない（SHALL）。コンテンツ利用者は、SCAPがサポートしないチェックシステムを実装してもよい（MAY）。ツールがサポートしないチェックシステムに遭遇した場合、警告を発しなければならず（MUST）、[XCCDF]仕様に従って処理を続行しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: When processing a patches-up-to-date rule, only OVAL patch class definitions SHALL be evaluated; all other classes of definitions (e.g., inventory class definitions) SHALL NOT be evaluated except when they serve, directly or indirectly, as criteria (extended definitions) of patch definitions.

contents.html: 4.5 XCCDF Results

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations pertain to content consumers generating XCCDF result data stream components.
contents.html_ja: 以下の要件と推奨事項は、XCCDF結果データストリーム構成要素を生成するコンテンツ利用者に適用される。

contents.html: Each XCCDF result data stream component SHALL comply with the XCCDF Results schema.
contents.html_ja: 各XCCDF結果データストリーム構成要素は、XCCDF Resultsスキーマに準拠するものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: XCCDF test results SHALL be documented as the contents of an <xccdf:TestResult> element. To be considered valid SCAP result content, the <xccdf:TestResult> element SHALL meet the following conditions:
contents.html_ja: XCCDFのテスト結果は、<xccdf:TestResult>要素の内容として記述するものとする（SHALL）。有効なSCAP結果コンテンツとみなされるためには、<xccdf:TestResult>要素は以下の条件を満たすものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: 1. The @start-time and @end-time attributes SHALL be provided to indicate when the scan started and completed, respectively.
contents.html_ja: 1. スキャンの開始時刻と完了時刻を示すため、それぞれ@start-time属性と@end-time属性を指定するものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: 2. The @test-system attribute SHALL be provided, and it SHALL be a CPE name value indicating the product that was responsible for generating the results.
contents.html_ja: 2. @test-system属性を指定するものとし（SHALL）、その値は、結果を生成した製品を示すCPE名とするものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: 3. When the <xccdf:TestResult> is the root XCCDF element, then it will include an <xccdf:benchmark> element [XCCDF:6.6.2]. The <xccdf:benchmark> element MUST have an @id attribute specified.
contents.html_ja: 3. <xccdf:TestResult>がルートのXCCDF要素である場合、<xccdf:benchmark>要素を含むことになる[XCCDF:6.6.2]。<xccdf:benchmark>要素には@id属性を指定しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: 4. Regarding the definition and use of <xccdf:Profile> elements, reported <xccdf:set-value> elements SHALL include all those values that are exported by the reported rules. The specific settings are those determined by the reported <xccdf:Profile>.
contents.html_ja: 4. <xccdf:Profile>要素の定義と使用に関して、報告される<xccdf:set-value>要素には、報告されるルールがエクスポートするすべての値を含めるものとする（SHALL）。具体的な設定値は、報告される<xccdf:Profile>によって決まる値である。

contents.html: 5. The <xccdf:identity> element SHALL identify the security principal used to access rule evaluation on the target(s). This will include the identity name or username used to perform the evaluation.
contents.html_ja: 5. <xccdf:identity>要素は、対象に対するルール評価のアクセスに使用したセキュリティプリンシパルを識別するものとする（SHALL）。これには、評価の実行に使用したID名またはユーザ名が含まれる。

contents.html: 6. Each IP address associated with the <xccdf:target> SHALL be enumerated using the <xccdf:target-address> element.
contents.html_ja: 6. <xccdf:target>に関連付けられた各IPアドレスは、<xccdf:target-address>要素を使用して列挙するものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: 7. An <xccdf:target-id-ref> SHALL be specified with a @system attribute of “http://scap.nist.gov/schema/asset-identification/1.1”, an @href attribute value of “”, and a @name attribute value of the ID of the <ai:asset> element in the ARF that this <xccdf:TestResult> is about.
contents.html_ja: 7. <xccdf:target-id-ref>を指定するものとし（SHALL）、その@system属性は「http://scap.nist.gov/schema/asset-identification/1.1」、@href属性の値は「」、@name属性の値は、この<xccdf:TestResult>が対象とするARF内の<ai:asset>要素のIDとする。

contents.html: 8. The <xccdf:rule-result> elements report the result of the application of each selected rule [XCCDF:6.6.2]. The <xccdf:check/xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL record the reference to the check system specific result component report ID and check name within the result file using the @href and @name attributes, respectively. The @href attribute SHALL contain “#” + the @id of the <arf:report> containing the check result. This approach provides traceability between XCCDF and check results. Note that if @multi-check is not set to “true” and the <xccdf:rule-result> represents a group of checks, then the @name attribute SHALL be omitted. This is a stripped down example:
contents.html_ja: 8. <xccdf:rule-result>要素は、選択された各ルールを適用した結果を報告する[XCCDF:6.6.2]。<xccdf:check/xccdf:check-content-ref>要素は、チェックシステム固有の結果構成要素レポートのIDと、結果ファイル内のチェック名への参照を、それぞれ@href属性と@name属性を使用して記録するものとする（SHALL）。@href属性には、「#」に続けて、チェック結果を含む<arf:report>の@idを含めるものとする（SHALL）。この方法により、XCCDFとチェック結果の間のトレーサビリティが確保される。なお、@multi-checkが「true」に設定されておらず、<xccdf:rule-result>がチェックのグループを表す場合、@name属性は省略するものとする（SHALL）。以下は、要素を絞り込んだ例である。

contents.html_ja: 4.5.1 ルール結果への識別子の割り当て

contents.html: The <xccdf:rule-result> element provides data indicating the result of assessing a system using the identified <xccdf:Rule> element. If the target <xccdf:Rule> identified by the <xccdf:rule-result> element’s @idref attribute has one or more <xccdf:ident> elements with a @system attribute value listed in Section 3.2.4.1, then each <xccdf:ident> element SHALL also appear within the <xccdf:rule-result> element.

If an <xccdf:ident> element is present and it identifies a CVE, CCE, or CPE entry, then an <xccdf:rule-result> of “pass” SHALL indicate that the check content evaluated within the rule complied with one of the following:

contents.html: For a CVE entry, the target platform satisfies all the conditions of the XCCDF rule and is unaffected by the vulnerability or exposure referenced by the CVE.
contents.html_ja: CVEエントリの場合、対象プラットフォームはXCCDFルールのすべての条件を満たし、CVEが参照する脆弱性または曝露の影響を受けない。

contents.html: For a CCE entry, the target platform complies with the configuration setting guidance expressed in the XCCDF rule.
contents.html_ja: CCEエントリの場合、対象プラットフォームはXCCDFルールに示された構成設定のガイダンスに適合する。

contents.html:
• For a CPE entry, the target platform was identified on the system.

It is important that these interpretations of <xccdf:ident> elements be preserved. For example, consider two policy recommendations. One is that a particular piece of software be installed, and the second that another piece of software not be installed. Both rules for these policy recommendations could use the same CPE entry in their <xccdf:ident> elements. However, because the interpretation of a CPE entry is that a “pass” result indicates software was installed, the second policy recommendation’s rule would violate this. This can be corrected by using the @con:negate attribute, a Boolean attribute that inverts the rule result. The second rule could check for the software being installed and then negate that result, thus giving a result consistent in meaning with the first rule. For rules that cannot have their interpretations preserved through the use of the @con:negate attribute, an alternative is to have a CCE entry corresponding to the recommendation. Rules that do not use <xccdf:ident> elements have no such restrictions.
contents.html_ja:
• CPEエントリの場合、対象プラットフォームがシステム上で確認された。

<xccdf:ident>要素のこれらの解釈を維持することが重要である。たとえば、二つのポリシー推奨事項を考える。一つ目は特定のソフトウェアをインストールすることであり、二つ目は別のソフトウェアをインストールしないことである。これらのポリシー推奨事項に対するルールは、どちらも<xccdf:ident>要素で同じCPEエントリを使用できる。しかし、CPEエントリの解釈では「pass」結果はソフトウェアがインストールされていたことを示すため、二つ目のポリシー推奨事項のルールはこの解釈に反する。これは、ルール結果を反転するBoolean属性である@con:negate属性を使用して修正できる。二つ目のルールでソフトウェアがインストールされていることをチェックし、その結果を否定すれば、一つ目のルールと意味が一致する結果が得られる。@con:negate属性を使用しても解釈を維持できないルールについては、推奨事項に対応するCCEエントリを用意する方法がある。<xccdf:ident>要素を使用しないルールには、このような制約はない。

contents.html: 4.5.2 Mapping OVAL Results to XCCDF Results
contents.html_ja: 4.5.2 OVAL結果からXCCDF結果へのマッピング

contents.html: When evaluating an <xccdf:Rule> element that references an OVAL Definition, the <xccdf:rule-result> element SHALL be used to capture the result of this evaluation. This result SHALL be determined by evaluating the referenced OVAL Definition on a target host. The result value of an individual <xccdf:check> SHALL be mapped from the OVAL Definition result produced during evaluation. The corresponding <xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:result> value is then computed based on the result values of all relevant <xccdf:check> elements. (Normally only a single <xccdf:check> element is needed, but where an <xccdf:complex-check> element is used, there may be multiple results that must be combined, as outlined in the XCCDF specification.) While the OVAL specification permits limiting result status reporting, SCAP-conformant content SHALL include full status reporting, including Error, Unknown, Not Applicable, Not Evaluated, True, and False.
contents.html_ja: OVAL Definitionを参照する<xccdf:Rule>要素を評価する際には、その評価結果を記録するために<xccdf:rule-result>要素を使用するものとする（SHALL）。この結果は、参照されるOVAL Definitionを対象ホスト上で評価することによって決定するものとする（SHALL）。個々の<xccdf:check>の結果値は、評価中に生成されたOVAL Definitionの結果から対応付けるものとする（SHALL）。対応する<xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:result>の値は、関連するすべての<xccdf:check>要素の結果値に基づいて算出される。（通常は1つの<xccdf:check>要素だけで足りるが、<xccdf:complex-check>要素を使用する場合は、XCCDF仕様に示されているとおり、複数の結果を組み合わせる必要がありうる。）OVAL仕様は結果状態の報告を限定することを認めているが、SCAPに準拠したコンテンツは、Error、Unknown、Not Applicable、Not Evaluated、True、Falseを含む完全な状態報告を含むものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: Content consumers SHALL apply the mapping illustrated in Table 21 when deriving <xccdf:check> results from OVAL Definition processing. The corresponding result value SHALL be recorded based on the @class attribute of the OVAL Definition where applicable.
contents.html_ja: コンテンツ利用者は、OVAL Definitionの処理から<xccdf:check>の結果を導出する際に、表21に示す対応付けを適用するものとする（SHALL）。対応する結果値は、該当する場合、OVAL Definitionの@class属性に基づいて記録するものとする（SHALL）。

contents.html: Table 21 - Deriving XCCDF Check Results from OVAL Definition Results
contents.html_ja: 表21 - OVAL Definitionの結果からのXCCDFチェック結果の導出

contents.html: OVAL Definition Result XCCDF Check Result error error unknown unknown not applicable notapplicable not evaluated notchecked Definition Class Definition Result compliance true vulnerability false Pass inventory true patch false Definition Class Definition Result compliance false vulnerability true Fail inventory false patch true
contents.html_ja: OVAL定義の結果／XCCDFチェックの結果：error → error、unknown → unknown、not applicable → notapplicable、not evaluated → notchecked。定義クラス／定義結果：compliance true、vulnerability false、inventory true、patch false → Pass。定義クラス／定義結果：compliance false、vulnerability true、inventory false、patch true → Fail。

contents.html: The mappings in Table 21 are specific to each OVAL Definition class. For example, if an OVAL compliance class definition is processed and OVAL returns a result of “true”, the content consumer is conveying the fact that the system was found to be compliant with that check and therefore returns a “pass” result for that check. A similar definition for a vulnerable condition will return results of “false” if that vulnerability was not found on the examined devices, resulting in a “pass” from the XCCDF check. Negations of check results or their combination in complex-checks may result in additional modification before the final corresponding <xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:result> value is known.
contents.html_ja: 表21のマッピングはOVAL定義の各クラス固有である。たとえば、OVALコンプライアンスクラス定義が処理され、OVALが“true”を返す場合、コンテンツ利用者はシステムがそのチェックに適合していると判断されたことを示し、そのチェックの結果として“pass”を返す。同様に、脆弱性条件の定義では、検査対象デバイスに脆弱性が見つからなければ“false”が返り、XCCDFチェックでは“pass”となる。チェック結果の否定や複雑なチェックでの結果の組み合わせにより、対応する最終<xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:result>値が確定する前に、さらに修正が必要となる場合がある。

contents.html: If the <xccdf:Rule> element under evaluation has an <xccdf:check-content-ref> element with the @name attribute omitted and an <xccdf:check> element with its @multi-check attribute set to “true”, then the result of each evaluated OVAL Definition SHALL be recorded as a separate <xccdf:rule-result> element. In this case the <xccdf:rule-result/xccdf:check-content-ref> element SHALL identify the specific check result of each evaluated OVAL Definition using the @href and @name attributes as described in Section 4.5, item 8.
4.6 OVAL Results
contents.html_ja: 4.6 OVAL結果

contents.html: The following requirements and recommendations pertain to content consumers generating OVAL result data stream components.
Each OVAL result data stream component SHALL validate against version 5.10 of the OVAL Results schema19 regardless of the version of the OVAL Definitions document that was evaluated.
An SCAP OVAL result data stream component SHALL include the results of every OVAL Definition used to generate the reported results.

In order to be SCAP conformant, an SCAP content consumer SHALL be able to produce all the types of OVAL Results output described below. The specific result output SHALL be configurable within the SCAP content consumer.

In order to support SCAP instances where OVAL thin content (only the ID of the definition and the results) is preferred, SCAP content consumers SHALL support all valid values for the <oval-res:directives> controlling the expected content of the results file.

To support the ability for results to be consumed by the appropriate product(s), data results SHALL be expressed as Single Machine Without System Characteristics, Single Machine With System Characteristics, or Single Machine With Thin Results as follows:

1. Single Machine Without System Characteristics – A single result file that includes the results of all OVAL Definitions evaluated and “full” results types as described in the <oval-res:ContentEnumeration> element, without system characteristics.
For this format, the values for the <oval-res:directives> element SHALL be:

<oval-res:directives include_source_definitions="false"> <oval-res:definition_true content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_false content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_unknown content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_error content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_evaluated content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_applicable content="full" reported="true"/> </oval-res:directives>

When creating the OVAL System Characteristics as defined by the <oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics> element, the <oval-sc:collected_objects> and <oval-sc:system_data> elements SHALL NOT be provided.

2. Single Machine With System Characteristics – A single result file that includes the results of all OVAL Definitions evaluated and “full” results types as described in the <oval-res:ContentEnumeration> element and the System Characteristics of the target evaluated.
For this format, the values for the <oval-res:directives> element SHALL be:
<oval-res:directives include_source_definitions="false">

19 The OVAL schemas are described in detail at http://oval.mitre.org/language/about. <oval-res:definition_true content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_false content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_unknown content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_error content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_evaluated content="full" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_applicable content="full" reported="true"/> </oval-res:directives>

contents.html: When creating the OVAL System Characteristics as defined by the <oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics> element, the <oval-sc:collected_objects> and <oval-sc:system_data> elements SHALL be provided.

3. Single Machine With Thin Results – A single result file that includes the results of all OVAL Definitions evaluated and “thin” results types as described in the OVAL Results schema. A value of “thin” means only the minimal amount of information will be provided.
For this format, the values for the <oval-res:directives> element SHALL be:

<oval-res:directives include_source_definitions="false"> <oval-res:definition_true content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_false content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_unknown content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_error content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_evaluated content="thin" reported="true"/> <oval-res:definition_not_applicable content="thin" reported="true"/> </oval-res:directives>

When specifying OVAL system characteristics, a reference SHOULD be made to the target asset in the ARF report collection. Specifically, the <oval-sc:oval_system_characteristics>/<oval-sc:system_info>/##any SHOULD be populated with a <con:asset-identification> element. That element MUST be populated with a single <arf:object-ref> element that points to the <ai:asset> element in the ARF report collection pertaining to the OVAL result. See [ARF] for details on populating the <arf:object-ref> element.
4.7 OCIL Results
The following requirements and recommendations pertain to content consumers generating OCIL result data stream components.
An SCAP OCIL result data stream component SHALL include the results of every <ocil:questionnaire>, <ocil:question_test_action>, and <ocil:question> element used to generate the reported results.
4.8 Result Data Stream Signing

Digitally signing result data stream content is important to ensuring the integrity and trustworthiness of results. Leveraging [TMSAD] for SCAP can improve the legitimacy of results of SCAP content and create a more secure environment. As such, content consumers MAY digitally sign result content following the guidelines in [TMSAD], along with the following requirements.

One XML digital signature MAY be included in an <arf:extended-info> element in the ARF report. The signature MUST be represented as a <dsig:Signature> element and MUST follow the W3C recommendation [DSIG]. The <dsig:Signature> element MUST sign the ARF report collection root element.
The <dsig:Signature> element MUST follow the recommendations in [TMSAD] and these additional requirements:
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Signature>要素は[TMSAD]の推奨事項と以下の追加要件に従わなければならない（MUST）：

contents.html: A <dsig:SignatureProperties> element MUST be included in the <dsig:Signature> element. At least one <dsig:SignatureProperty> element MUST be populated with <dt:signature-info> as specified in [TMSAD].
contents.html_ja: <dsig:SignatureProperties>要素を<dsig:Signature>要素内に含めなければならない（MUST）。少なくとも一つの<dsig:SignatureProperty>要素に、[TMSAD]で指定された<dt:signature-info>を設定しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: The first <dsig:Reference> element in a <dsig:Signature> element MUST be to the <arf:asset-report-collection> element. The element MUST be referenced in the @URI attribute using the empty string convention “”.
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Signature>要素内の最初の<dsig:Reference>要素は<arf:asset-report-collection>要素を参照しなければならない（MUST）。同要素は、空文字列規約“”を用いて参照しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: Two XPath Filter 2 transforms MUST exist on the first <dsig:Reference> element in a <dsig:Signature> element. Both MUST specify a filter type of “subtract”. The first transform MUST specify the XPath “/arf:asset-report-collection/arf:extended-infos[count(arf:extended-info[dsig:Signature]) = count(*)]”. The second transform MUST specify the XPath “/arf:asset-report-collection/arf:extended-infos/arf:extended-info[dsig:Signature]”. In both cases, the namespace prefix “arf” MUST map to the ARF namespace specified in this document.
contents.html_ja: <dsig:Signature>要素内の最初の<dsig:Reference>要素には、二つのXPath Filter 2変換が存在しなければならない（MUST）。両方のfilter型は“subtract”でなければならない（MUST）。第一の変換ではXPath “/arf:asset-report-collection/arf:extended-infos[count(arf:extended-info[dsig:Signature]) = count(*)]”を指定しなければならない（MUST）。第二の変換ではXPath “/arf:asset-report-collection/arf:extended-infos/arf:extended-info[dsig:Signature]”を指定しなければならない（MUST）。いずれの場合も、namespace prefix “arf”は本書で指定するARF名前空間に対応付けなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: The second <dsig:Reference> element MUST be to the <dsig:SignatureProperties> element captured in a <dsig:Object> element with the <dsig:Signature> element. The <dsig:SignatureProperties> element MUST be referenced in the @URI attribute using “#” + @Id of the <dsig:SignatureProperties> element.
contents.html_ja: 第二の<dsig:Reference>要素は、<dsig:Signature>要素内の<dsig:Object>要素に格納された<dsig:SignatureProperties>要素を参照しなければならない（MUST）。<dsig:SignatureProperties>要素は、“#” + <dsig:SignatureProperties>要素の@Idを用いて@URI属性内で参照しなければならない（MUST）。

contents.html: Key information SHOULD be provided on the <dsig:Signature> element.
contents.html_ja: 鍵情報は<dsig:Signature>要素に指定すべきである（SHOULD）。

contents.html: In situations where it is desirable to countersign a result data stream (e.g., when a content consumer automatically signs a result data stream and then a person also wants to sign the results), the following requirements apply.

contents.html: The <arf:extended-info> element containing the original signature SHALL be removed from the resulting document.
